title: Healthcare Call Center Metrics: Benchmarks and Cost per Call for Specialty Practices
summary: Track 7 healthcare call center metrics for your specialty practice. Get abandonment, wait time, and cost per call benchmarks and how to improve them.
body_markdown:
Your phone report counts the calls your team answered. The calls that ended before anyone picked up leave no record, and each one is a visit your practice did not book.


Healthcare call center metrics are the measures a specialty practice uses to judge phone access: call abandonment rate, average speed of answer, service level, first call resolution, patient satisfaction, after-hours answer rate, and cost per call. Together they show how many patients reach your team and what each call costs.


## TL;DR


- Under 5% is the common call abandonment goal, and general call center averages run about 7%, per[HFMA](https://www.hfma.org/revenue-cycle/kpis/7256/) .
- 18% of daytime calls and 81% of after-hours calls go unanswered at specialty practices, per[Prosper AI's 2026 Growth Report](https://www.getprosper.ai/report/specialty-revenue-growth-2026) .
- Cost per call is monthly phone operating cost divided by calls handled. A[published study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7393684/) of a large urology practice found $4.02 per call for its internal call center and $3.59 for an outsourced one.
- A booked visit is not a paid visit: practices average 10% of first-submission claims denied, per[Prosper AI's 2026 Growth Report](https://www.getprosper.ai/report/specialty-revenue-growth-2026) .


## What call center metrics should healthcare organizations track to reduce call abandonment and improve patient satisfaction?


Track seven metrics: call abandonment rate, average speed of answer, service level, first call resolution, patient satisfaction, after-hours answer rate, and cost per call. The first three show whether patients reach you. The last four show whether the call worked and what it cost. Start with abandonment, because it counts the patients you lost.


1. **Call abandonment rate:** the share of inbound calls that end before a person answers.
2. **Average speed of answer (ASA):** the average seconds from first ring to a live answer.
3. **Service level:** the share of calls answered within a set time, such as 80% within 20 seconds.
4. **First call resolution (FCR):** the share of requests finished on the first call.
5. **Patient satisfaction:** a post-call survey score or the access questions in CG-CAHPS.
6. **After-hours answer rate:** the share of calls outside office hours that reach a resolution.
7. **Cost per call:** total phone operating cost divided by calls handled.


## What is a good call abandonment rate in healthcare?


A good call abandonment rate is under 5%.[HFMA](https://www.hfma.org/revenue-cycle/kpis/7256/) lists under 5% as the goal and 7% as the general call center average, and the[Children's Hospital Association](https://www.childrenshospitals.org/news/childrens-hospitals-today/2021/02/dont-overlook-your-hospitals-phone-system) cites 5% as the industry benchmark. Treat 5% as your ceiling and measure it by location and by hour, because a blended average hides peak-hour losses.

HFMA states its call center standards are general and not specific to healthcare, and that patient calls take more time on the phone.


The Children's Hospital Association reports Nemours saw abandonment spikes in the 30% range before it simplified its phone tree. The average held at 8% in 2019 and about 3% in 2020.


## What is a good average speed of answer and hold time for a medical practice?


[HFMA](https://www.hfma.org/revenue-cycle/kpis/7256/) cites 67 seconds as a general average wait and a service level goal of 80% of calls answered within 20 seconds. HFMA also notes these standards are not healthcare specific. Set your own target from your abandonment curve: find the wait where callers start hanging up, then staff to stay under it.


Build that curve in four steps:


1. Pull four weeks of data from your call queue report, not the missed-call view of a single phone line.
2. Split abandonment and answer speed by hour and weekday.
3. Mark the wait time where abandonment climbs.
4. Compare each peak hour with the 20-second service level goal.


Answered callers still wait. Per[Prosper AI's 2026 Growth Report](https://www.getprosper.ai/report/specialty-revenue-growth-2026) , answered callers wait 1.5 minutes on average and 20% are held more than 5 minutes.


## How do first call resolution and patient satisfaction connect to call abandonment?


Abandonment counts the patients who hung up. First call resolution and patient satisfaction describe what happened to the patients who stayed. A practice with low abandonment and low first call resolution still creates callbacks, and callbacks refill the queue. Track all three together and review them by call type.


Phone access is a priority for practice leaders. In[MGMA's December 2025 poll](https://www.mgma.com/mgma-stat/patient-access-priorities-for-2026) of 236 respondents, 22% named phone access as their top patient access priority, behind no-shows (27%) and online scheduling (24%).


Call types with the most repeat calls are the place to look first: scheduling changes, benefits questions, and balance questions.


## Which sources should you trust for healthcare call center benchmarks?


Use HFMA, MGMA, and AHRQ as reference points, and treat vendor blogs as opinion. HFMA publishes call center KPI standards. MGMA DataDive lists call hold time, answer speed, and abandonment rate as call center benchmarks. AHRQ's CAHPS improvement guide includes[standards for customer service](https://www.ahrq.gov/cahps/quality-improvement/improvement-guide/6-strategies-for-improving/customer-service/strategy6q-custservice-standards.html) . Then baseline your own queue.


## How much does a call cost a specialty practice?


Cost per call equals your monthly phone operating cost divided by calls handled. A[published study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7393684/) of a large urology community practice found $4.02 per call for its internal call center and $3.59 for an outsourced one, with no statistically significant difference. Your number depends on call volume, staffing mix, and workflows, so calculate it from your own payroll, phone system, and call counts.


Those figures come from one practice that handled 134,799 calls in six months internally, so a smaller group may see a higher cost per call. The study measured total operating expenses divided by calls.


Calculate it in four steps:


1. Add monthly payroll and benefits for everyone who answers phones.
2. Add phone system, software, and quality assurance costs.
3. Divide the total by calls handled, not calls received.
4. Repeat the math by call type to find your most expensive calls.

[Prosper AI's 2026 Growth Report](https://www.getprosper.ai/report/specialty-revenue-growth-2026) values missed calls at $44.8K per physician per year, the largest of four revenue levers worth $125K per physician combined. The report found 18% of daytime calls go unanswered and 81% of after-hours calls go unanswered.

## What happens after the appointment is booked?


A booked visit is not a paid visit. Before the patient arrives, your team still verifies benefits, secures prior authorization, and fixes the errors that become denials. Prosper AI's agents make these patient and payer calls in the same workflow, so your schedule fills with financially cleared visits.


- **Benefits verification:** practices average 10% of first-submission claims denied, 22% in orthopedics and 16% in gastroenterology. The report values accurate benefit checks at $28.5K per physician per year, per[Prosper AI's 2026 Growth Report](https://www.getprosper.ai/report/specialty-revenue-growth-2026) .
- **Prior authorization:** physicians complete an average of 40 prior authorizations per week and spend 13 hours of physician and staff time on them, per the[AMA](https://www.ama-assn.org/press-center/ama-press-releases/ama-survey-prior-authorization-reform-pledge-falls-short-physicians) . A manual prior authorization costs $15.12 for specialists against $6.61 electronic, per the[2023 CAQH Index](https://www.caqh.org/hubfs/CAQH%20Insights_2023%20Index%20Report_Provider%20Specialty%20Issue%20Brief_Final.pdf) .
- **Denials:** MGMA puts the cost to rework a claim at about $25 and 71 minutes, as[reported by Becker's](https://www.beckershospitalreview.com/finance/how-to-prevent-claim-denials-and-bolster-the-bottom-line/) .
- **Payer calls:** Prosper AI's agents call payers directly, navigate phone trees, wait on hold, and log the result in your EHR.


Read more on[financially cleared appointments](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/financially-cleared-appointments-verifying-benefits) and[preventable claim denials](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/preventable-claim-denials-specialty-practices) .


## What does rollout look like across many locations?


Prosper AI deployments start with a limited call scope and expand as results hold. Per Prosper AI's positioning materials, go-live typically takes about three weeks and full ramp runs 10 to 12 weeks, with a dedicated implementation partner. Confirm timing for your EHR and locations during scoping.


A phased rollout follows five steps:


1. **Pick the call types:** start with high-volume scheduling or benefits calls.
2. **Run live test calls:** tune tone, terminology, and logic to your workflows.
3. **Launch one location or one call type:** compare abandonment and answer speed with your baseline.
4. **Review calls weekly:** refine escalation rules and staff handoffs.
5. **Expand across locations:** add call types and sites as results hold.

### Does Prosper AI cover prior authorization and benefits verification too?


Yes. Prosper AI covers benefits verification and prior authorization calls as well as scheduling and patient billing, so one platform runs the front and back office. Its agents call payers directly and write outcomes to your EHR. Confirm which call types and payers are live for your specialty during scoping.

Yes. Prosper AI deployments start small and scale. Northeast OB/GYN began with a limited scope, validated performance, refined escalation rules, and then expanded to new patient intake and insurance updates. Start with one location or one call type that has high volume and a measurable abandonment rate.
